title: DEV_BYPASS token comparison non-constant-time; no staging guard in vciso-service
description:
**Files:** `vciso-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts:344`
**Root Cause:** The `DEV_BYPASS` token validation uses JavaScript `===` operator for string comparison — a non-constant-time operation that enables a timing oracle attack. An attacker can enumerate the token character by character by measuring response times. Additionally, there is no hard guard preventing `DEV_BYPASS=true` from being accidentally set in staging.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vciso-service/src/plugins/keycloak.ts`, import `{ timingSafeEqual } from 'crypto'`. Replace the token comparison with: `const a = Buffer.from(token ?? ''); const b = Buffer.from(process.env.DEV_BYPASS_TOKEN ?? ''); if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) { ... }`. Add startup guard: `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' && process.env.DEV_BYPASS === 'true') throw new Error('DEV_BYPASS must not be enabled in production')`.
fixEvidence: CWE-208 / OWASP A05 — vciso-service/keycloak.ts:344 — timing oracle on shared token comparison

title: Internal audit-log endpoint fails open when INTERNAL_SECRET is unset
statusRaw: 🟢 FIXED — reverified 2026-08-02 while authoring Logs system test cases
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/activity/activity-log.routes.js:14-16`
**Root Cause (as originally found):** The guard used `if (INTERNAL_SECRET && req.headers['x-internal-secret'] !== INTERNAL_SECRET)`. Because `INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET` was not set in `.env`, `INTERNAL_SECRET` was falsy, causing the condition to short-circuit to false — meaning the guard never fired. Any caller could inject arbitrary audit log entries without any credentials.
**Claude Fix Prompt (as originally written):**
In `activity-log.routes.js` at line 16, change the guard to: `if (!INTERNAL_SECRET || req.headers['x-internal-secret'] !== INTERNAL_SECRET) { return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }); }`. Also define `INTERNAL_SERVICE_SECRET` with a cryptographically random value in all environment configurations and AWS Secrets Manager.
fixEvidence: Confirmed fixed by direct code read 2026-08-02: activity-log.routes.js:14-16 now reads `if (!INTERNAL_SECRET || req.headers['x-internal-secret'] !== INTERNAL_SECRET) { return res.status(401)... }` with an inline comment "fail closed: reject if secret is unset OR header doesn't match" — exactly the originally-prescribed fix.

title: DEV_BYPASS hardcodes real production MongoDB orgId and userId
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/authenticate.js:22-25`
**Root Cause:** The DEV_BYPASS block hardcodes real MongoDB `orgId` (`6897584a54a19172fda820b6`) and `userId` (`6900e3193bd49775683e2d5b`) — values that correspond to real production accounts. If `DEV_BYPASS=true` is accidentally set on a public server, any unauthenticated request accesses a real production account with that user's permissions.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/authenticate.js`, replace the hardcoded real IDs in the DEV_BYPASS block with synthetic test values: `organizationId: '000000000000000000000000'` and `userId: '000000000000000000000001'`. Add a startup assertion: `if (process.env.DEV_BYPASS === 'true' && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') throw new Error('DEV_BYPASS must not be enabled in production')`.
fixEvidence: CWE-798 / OWASP A02 — authenticate.js:22-25 — real orgId/userId in source; if DEV_BYPASS accidentally on → real account accessed

title: 3-hour Redis cache means revoked permissions active for up to 3 hours
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/loadPermissions.js`
**Root Cause:** Permission resolution results are cached in Redis with a 3-hour TTL (`AUTHZ_TTL_MS`). When an organization administrator revokes a user's role or removes a permission, the change does not take effect until the cache expires — up to 3 hours later. During this window, the revoked user retains all previously granted permissions.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add a cache invalidation mechanism to the role/permission update endpoints. In the RBAC controller (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/rbac/`), after any role update or user permission change, call `cache.del(\`authz:${orgId}:${userId}\`)` for affected users. Also reduce `AUTHZ_TTL_MS` to 30 minutes (1800000) as a defense-in-depth measure. Document the eventual-consistency window in `RBAC_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`.
fixEvidence: CWE-613 / OWASP A07 — loadPermissions.js — AUTHZ_TTL_MS = 3h; no cache invalidation on role change

title: INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN grants SUPERADMIN access without per-request audit trail
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/authenticate.js` (service-to-service path)
**Root Cause:** Requests authenticated via the `x-service-token` header receive `req.userRoles = [{ systemRoleKey: 'SUPERADMIN' }]`, bypassing all `requirePermission` checks. These requests are logged only with `req.userId = 'service-account'` — there is no resource-level audit trail showing which service performed which operation, making post-incident forensics difficult.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Enhance service-to-service authentication to require a service identity header: `x-service-name`. Set `req.userId = \`service:\${req.headers['x-service-name'] || 'unknown'}\`` for more specific audit trail attribution. Add AuditLog entries for all state-mutating service-to-service operations. Consider replacing the shared INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN with per-service tokens.
fixEvidence: CWE-269 / OWASP A01 — authenticate.js (s2s path) — service-to-service calls logged as 'service-account' with no resource-level audit

title: ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS=false disables all permission checks globally
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/requirePermission.js`
**Root Cause:** If `ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS === 'false'` in a non-production environment, all calls to `requirePermission()`, `requireAnyPermission()`, and `requireAllPermissions()` are no-ops that immediately call `next()`. If this env var is accidentally set in a staging environment accessible to external users, the entire RBAC model is disabled for that environment.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add a startup assertion in `vibrantix-backend/src/index.js`: `if (process.env.ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS === 'false' && process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'development') { throw new Error('ENFORCE_PERMISSIONS=false is only allowed in NODE_ENV=development'); }`. Add a log warning at startup whenever ENFORCE is disabled so it is visible in monitoring.
fixEvidence: CWE-284 / OWASP A01 — requirePermission.js — if env var accidentally set in staging, entire RBAC disabled
